analyst_view.overall: Early view: a big derby between Fenerbahce (6th), who have had a turbulent autumn (Ismail Kartal resigned, Dirk Kuyt was interim coach and Emre Belozoglu has now taken over, starting with a 5-0 win at Corum), and Trabzonspor (2nd), who have won six league games in a row under Thomas Reis and have the league's best defence. Both play in Europe that week: Fenerbahce away at LASK in the Champions League on 9 December and Trabzonspor at home to Jablonec in the Conference League on 10 December, so Trabzonspor get one day less rest.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.5 goals. I lean lower: Trabzonspor have conceded only 8 in 11 league games and 3 in their six-game winning run, and big derbies tend to be tighter than the teams' scoring records suggest, even with Fenerbahce the league's top scorers.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.2 corners. Fenerbahce at home should have long spells of pressure, but Trabzonspor have been strong in transition under Reis; nothing I found moves this either way.

cards.text: The numbers say 6.7 cards. I lean higher: this is one of the league's fiercest rivalries, both teams are fighting for the top places, and there is new-coach pressure at Fenerbahce. Tired legs after midweek European games can also mean more late fouls.

shots.text: The numbers say 30.8 shots. Fenerbahce's attack has been the best in the league and Belozoglu wants more organisation, but Trabzonspor rarely give much away; I stay with the numbers for now.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.9 shots on target. I lean slightly lower because Trabzonspor's defence has kept most opponents quiet this season and the midweek European games for both sides may lead to some rotation and a more cautious game.
